answer.rationale: Latency spike on the write path coincides temporally with the release 2 hours ago. memory_b1 shows rollback is an effective tool for release-induced errors and can complete without customer impact. memory_b2 is critical to review because regional failover is ruled out: settlement traffic is at peak with heavy writes, and memory_b2 explicitly warns against failover during hot writes due to replication gap risk and write loss. memory_b4 and memory_b6 document that staged gating and circuit breakers work well but cannot directly address write-path latency caused by a bad release. The constraint of one intervention, the timing correlation, and the customer write protection requirement all favor rollback. The release is the most likely root cause and rollback has the highest confidence outcome. Verifying memory_b1 (rollback safety) and memory_b2 (failover danger) will confirm both why rollback is the right choice and why failover is not.
